reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, the full StructureDefinition report, the deterministic aggregate only after forming the resource-level judgment, direct behavior findings whose affectedResources include `ResearchElementDefinition`, and shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior only as non-scoring context. I also checked the local R4/R6 package definitions for the missing R6 same-name StructureDefinition and the key R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` versus R6 `EvidenceVariable` element shapes.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` was trial-use/FMM 0, so there is weak standards pressure to preserve the exact resource identity or every old path in base R6. That weakens the case for retaining a duplicate obsolete resource, but it does not make the migration unimportant because the resource can encode evidence and recommendation semantics such as population, exposure, outcome, criteria, timing, and formal logic links.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 removes `ResearchElementDefinition`, and the likely `EvidenceVariable` path is a semantic remodel, so resource-level migration dominates; mapping and API transition guidance remain important but old-field preservation is not the main lever.

reasoning.thesisMd: `ResearchElementDefinition` is not a same-resource evolution with isolated element breaks. The R6 core package has no same-name StructureDefinition and lists the name as an old FHIR type, so any R4 instance, generated model, canonical profile reference, REST endpoint, or search base using this resource needs a resource-level migration before R6 validation or routing can work.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The practical migration shape is a removed/replaced resource with a semantic remodel into the evidence domain, most plausibly involving R6 `EvidenceVariable` plus `Evidence.variableDefinition`, `Group`, or extensions depending on use. A mechanical rename is not sufficient: R4 `type` and `variableType` encode PICO role and variable handling, while R4's mandatory `characteristic` backbone with required `definition[x]` does not survive as a same-path R6 model. Optional metadata such as `subject[x]`, `library`, comments, related artifacts, usage, jurisdiction, topic, and subtitle also require explicit mapping policy.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A migration program is unavoidable and dominates planning because the resource identity itself is gone. For this particular FMM 0 resource, the obvious base-compatible alternatives are not low-cost: retaining a deprecated `ResearchElementDefinition` resource or duplicating the old `type` and `characteristic` structures inside the successor would require validators, SDKs, search, endpoint behavior, documentation, and conflict/precedence rules for a retired duplicate evidence model. Preventing additional breaks still has value where it is cheap, especially through authoritative mappings, examples, endpoint/search transition guidance, and possibly implementation-specific aliases, but those actions reduce migration risk rather than avoiding the resource-level migration.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: No clearly cheap base-compatible field preservation was identified. A deprecated compatibility resource would preserve old payloads but would effectively keep the obsolete model alive. A retained PICO role field or old `characteristic` backbone would overlap with R6 `Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole`, `EvidenceVariable.definition`, definition modifiers, timing, constraints, and missing-data semantics. More modest actions such as a ConceptMap/StructureMap, successor-resource narrative, and search/endpoint transition metadata are standards-review-worthy, but they are migration aids rather than designs that make R4 instances valid as R6 base resources.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior findings are in scope and reinforce the same conclusion. The base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises a `ResearchElementDefinition` REST endpoint, and search parameters whose only R4 base was this removed resource disappear from the R6 search surface. These are concrete runtime/conformance breaks for generic clients, but they are derivative of the resource identity removal. Shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` operation/search changes were considered only as ecosystem context because this review is not for the base resources themselves.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate that major migration is already unavoidable, the shape is `removed-or-replaced-resource`, and the practical compatibility posture is `migration-program-dominates`. The nuance is that this should not be read as no action needed: the successor ambiguity, terminology/criteria mapping, and endpoint/search transition still deserve explicit standards guidance even though retaining old element names is not the highest-leverage compatibility strategy.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high that the same-name R6 resource is absent and that raw R4 instances cannot validate as R6. Confidence is only medium for exact successor mapping because the supplied local material did not include an official HL7 migration note, ConceptMap, StructureMap, ballot rationale, rendered narrative review, or terminology-server expansions.

findingConsiderations.title: ResearchElementDefinition resource is absent from the R6 core package
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive resource-level break. An R4 instance with `resourceType` `ResearchElementDefinition` has no same-name R6 base StructureDefinition, so validation, generated classes, server routing, CapabilityStatement declarations, canonical profile references, and endpoint/search behavior all require a top-level migration before local element compatibility can help.

findingConsiderations.title: Closest R6 successor is EvidenceVariable, but the match is semantic rather than a one-to-one rename
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the main standards-review-worthy uncertainty. `EvidenceVariable` has related purpose text, but R4 already had a separate `EvidenceVariable` and some R4 role semantics appear to move into `Evidence.variableDefinition`; without official guidance, converters may choose different destinations and silently alter population, exposure, outcome, criteria, or evidence-context meaning.

findingConsiderations.title: Required PICO type and variableType code model has no direct R6 EvidenceVariable equivalent
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The mandatory R4 PICO `type` and optional `variableType` are central to evidence interpretation and generated enum logic, so migration tests and mapping rules are necessary. Still, R6 has plausible alternative homes in `Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole` and `EvidenceVariable.handling`, and preserving the old fields in base R6 would duplicate role/handling semantics rather than cheaply avoid the resource redesign.

findingConsiderations.title: Mandatory characteristic backbone was replaced by a different optional EvidenceVariable definition model
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shows that the replacement is not merely a resource-name change. Every valid R4 instance has at least one `characteristic`, and migrating criteria, exclusions, timing, units, and conjunction semantics into the R6 definition/modifier/constraint model requires explicit mapping policy. It is safety-significant content, but retaining the old backbone alongside the richer R6 criteria model would create competing representations and precedence problems.

findingConsiderations.title: Several optional ResearchElementDefinition metadata and relationship fields are removed or reshaped in the likely successor
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Subject context, Library references, relationships, comments, and other optional metadata can matter for CDS/evidence interpretation and auditability. Because these fields are optional on an FMM 0 retired resource and many have transform or extension strategies, they are best treated as migration-map requirements rather than reasons to preserve the whole old resource shape.

findingConsiderations.title: Successor status is optional, creating R6-to-R4 and runtime assumptions risk
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This does not make valid R4 instances invalid in forward migration because all R4 instances already contain `status` and R6 can still carry it. It is mainly a reverse-conversion or governance-policy issue for new R6 `EvidenceVariable` instances that omit status.

findingConsiderations.title: Summary representation changes for migrated EvidenceVariable content
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Summary flag differences can affect `_summary` projections and generated summary views, but they do not affect base instance validity and are secondary to the missing resource identity. For this FMM 0 retired resource, clients that need applicability periods or criteria should use explicit elements or full-resource retrieval after migration.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a direct `ResearchElementDefinition` API break: old resource-specific queries have no R6 base endpoint to execute against. It does not independently justify preserving the full old resource, but standards guidance should document replacement queries, redirects, or deprecated aliases where a successor endpoint is clear.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The missing base endpoint advertisement affects generic clients and conformance tools that derive route inventories from CapabilityStatement. For `ResearchElementDefinition`, this is derivative of the accepted resource removal, but endpoint replacement metadata and transition notes would reduce runtime migration surprises.

findingConsiderations.title: Required input parameter renamed from `input` to `resource`
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Shared `Resource` operation changes may affect conversion tooling used during migration, but they are not specific to `ResearchElementDefinition` and were not counted in the resource-level migration conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The shared special search-parameter metadata changes are relevant background for client migration generally, but they apply to `Resource`/`DomainResource` as base behavior and should not be duplicated as a `ResearchElementDefinition`-specific break.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish an explicit R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` migration guide, ConceptMap, or StructureMap covering resource identity, canonical/profile references, `type`, `variableType`, `characteristic.definition[x]`, exclusions, timing, units, subject context, Library links, related artifacts, metadata, and known R6-to-R4 lossiness.
Clarify the intended successor pattern with examples: when old content should become an R6 `EvidenceVariable`, an `Evidence.variableDefinition`, a `Group`, an extension, or a combination.

Document endpoint and search-parameter transitions for retired `ResearchElementDefinition` REST/search surfaces, including deprecated aliases or redirects only where the successor semantics are unambiguous and implementation cost is acceptable.

Add migration validation examples for PICO role mapping, variable handling codes, criteria/conjunction semantics, exclusions, timing, units, subject default handling, Library references, and status preservation.

Consider a deprecated compatibility resource/profile only if external implementation evidence shows substantial production reliance; based on the supplied FMM 0 context, retaining the whole old resource in base R6 is not the default recommendation.

caveats: No official HL7 migration note, ConceptMap, StructureMap, rendered diff, or ballot rationale for `ResearchElementDefinition` removal was supplied.
The review infers `EvidenceVariable` and related R6 evidence-domain structures as likely successors from local package definitions and reports; exact successor policy remains uncertain.
Terminology-server expansions and rendered narrative pages/examples were not reviewed here.
Shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` behavior findings were treated as context only, not as `ResearchElementDefinition`-specific direct behavior findings.
